scope: Source retrieval only; no installation, hook enablement, runtime execution, behavioral eval or automatic cultural judgment.

candidate.name: impeccable
candidate.counting_note: One real skill entrypoint with multiple command/reference playbooks and generated provider copies; count once, not once per command/provider.
actual_contents: Context loader reads product/design/surface context. Explicit brief and pinned aesthetics override saturated-pattern warnings.
Modes distinguish persuade, operate, read and experience. Portfolio/gallery is explicitly experience.
Command playbooks cover typography, color, layout, animation, art direction, critique, accessibility/performance and live iteration.
Craft-floor guidance is loaded before UI edits; bounded QA instructions limit rounds.
Hook management and drift repair are explicit commands; source forbids opportunistic drift repair during ordinary design work.
candidate.relevance_fact: General frontend craft, not a Japanese-specific aesthetics pack; user-pinned eras/materials/fonts/palettes explicitly win over anti-pattern warnings.
candidate.possible_use_inference: Could supply existing general craft and mechanical checks beside separately authored Japanese-specific principles; this is applicability inference, not selection or validation.

hook.implementation: Rust native engine; post-edit regex source detector and static-HTML DOM/CSS detector, plus session cache/dedup and completion scan.
automatic_behavior: Matches Claude Edit/Write and Codex Edit/Write/apply_patch; source normalization extracts apply_patch paths.
Per-edit pass scans touched supported UI files. Default immediate tier includes mechanical defects and selected anti-patterns; copy/palette/type/layout taste heuristics are deferred to Stop.
Stop performs full-rule pass on touched files, deduplicates earlier findings, observes recursion guard, and can suppress verified preexisting text findings with before-edit baselines.
Hook output provides findings/correction prompts, optional clean/pending acknowledgements, context freshness notes and build-completion reminders.
Hook does not automatically repair code, write ignore exceptions, certify visual quality, or judge Japanese cultural authenticity.
hook.what_is_not_proven: The detector uses heuristics, regex and static HTML analysis; inspected hook path does not run a screenshot-based art-direction judge. Broad craft/reflexes remain agent-guided. No skill/hook quality eval was run here.

codex.source_manifest_path_caution: Checked-in source template still refers to .codex/skills/impeccable; installer rewrites the command for .agents provider. Do not blindly copy that stale launcher path.
codex.requires_user_step: Project trusted configuration and first-time hook approval through /hooks, according to bundled README/reference.
codex.response_shape: PostToolUse uses hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext. Nonempty Codex Stop output uses top-level decision:block and reason to continue the turn; it does not undo/block the already-completed edit.

claude.install_target: .claude/settings.local.json (project-local, gitignored); shared settings.json respected if already used
claude.response_shape: Additional context after edits and at completion; no pre-edit rejection.
claude.execution_note: Bundled README states installed command hooks run independently of model-tool approval; first Edit/Stop may therefore fetch/cache native engine even when model launcher execution is denied.

cursor.behavior: Separate hook-before-edit implementation examines proposed writes and can deny writes when detector finds issues. This blocking behavior must not be attributed to Claude/Codex PostToolUse.

hook.portability_summary: Skill sources are generated for many providers; event schemas/paths and trust differ. Codex and Claude require provider-native manifests, not one interchangeable JSON. Native-platform projects skip this web detector hook.

configuration.behavior: on installs/repairs manifests and records local consent. enabled:false disables automatic hook; manual detect unaffected. quiet:true silences clean/pending acknowledgement. Configured ignores affect manual and hook scans unless explicitly bypassed.
configuration.exceptions: Source allows narrow evidence-backed ignore-value exceptions; broad ignore-file/ignore-rule requires user request. Hook itself does not write exception config.

execution_prerequisites.runtime: Self-contained native engine; Node is unnecessary for skill launcher/hook. npx installation route needs Node only for npx.
execution_prerequisites.first_run: Prefer configured/bundled/preinstalled native binary; otherwise launcher downloads pinned engine release into ~/.impeccable/bin/<version>/.
requires: Network and writable cache when binary absent
shasum or sha256sum for first-download verification; cmd sibling for Windows
execution_prerequisites.verification_behavior: Fresh download requires matching .sha256 sidecar; missing sidecar/hash tool/mismatch refuses execution. Trusted configured/bundled binaries and reusable cache are handled as launcher trust candidates rather than freshly authenticated downloads.
risks: Hooks invoke executables on provider events and can fetch/cache binaries during first invocation.
Mechanical/static heuristics can report style preferences or miss rendered behavior; output is not proof of aesthetics/accessibility conformance.
Codex Stop decision:block may prolong an agent turn; hook recursion guard and dedup are source-inspected, not runtime-validated.
Provider checked-in template/installed launcher paths differ; installation mechanism must resolve actual project skill location.

additional_candidates.name: make-interfaces-feel-better
additional_candidates.summary: Concrete UI detail/polish guidance covering geometry, optical alignment, elevation versus structure, interruptible motion, type, icons, hit areas and evidence-bounded review.
actual_guidance: Keep existing styling system rather than introducing another one; inspect hover/focus/active/loading/empty states and review animation slowly.
Concentric nested radii; optical rather than purely geometric icon alignment; borders for structural/state cues and layered shadows for depth.
Interruptible transitions for state changes; staggers only for infrequent hierarchy-revealing entrances; subdued exits; no transition:all; will-change only when justified.
Specific prescriptions include icon scale0.25→1 / blur4px→0, press scale0.96, heading balance/body pretty, subtle pure-black/pure-white image outlines and icon stroke/text weight matching.
Prefer44×44 touch hit areas and at least40×40 dense desktop areas; avoid overlapping targets; motion requires static feedback too.
Quick/full review modes cap findings and require actual inspected evidence, rejected candidates and explicit unverified checks.
prerequisites: Instruction/reference skill with no executable hook found in repository tree.
HTML/CSS/browser work and access to relevant component source.
If motion/framer-motion is already present, use existing imports; otherwise icon transitions have a CSS fallback without added dependency.
risks: Prescriptive numeric/icon/image/type rules are authored design recipes, not universal cultural or accessibility proof.
The skill is general interaction polish, not Japanese aesthetic grounding.
Native text-wrap behavior and Japanese composition requirements need project/browser-specific checking rather than blanket application.
No behavioral evaluation, hook execution, installation or source change performed.

sources.finding: Established styling system and slow review of actual states.
Nineteen concrete craft and interaction principles.
Evidence-bounded review modes/output and unverified-check reporting.
